extracted.intended_audience: taxonomists, zoologists, museum curators, and systematic biologists working on freshwater sponges and phylactolaematous polyzoa
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and conventions for describing and illustrating new or known species in a taxonomic monograph, including diagnostic characters, comparisons with related taxa, type deposition, habitat/biology notes, and specimen/figure preparation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Species diagnostic characters
rubrics_metrics.description: A new species may be distinguished from a related species by explicit morphological characters (e.g. 'This species may be distinguished from S. indica by (i) its entirely recumbent zooecia, and (ii) the lateral branches of its zoarium').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give clear, enumerated characters that separate the taxon from the most similar species. Use direct comparisons to named taxa and list the minimal set of distinguishing features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zoarium structure and budding pattern
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe zoarium form (e.g. 'Zoarium entirely recumbent, consisting of zooecia joined together, often in groups of three, by slender, transparent, tubular processes'), including how processes are formed and relative growth of tubules and zooecia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report the arrangement and connections of zooecia, presence/absence of stolon-like tubules, patterns of budding (anterior daughter-zooecium, lateral daughter-zooecia), and how colony morphology changes with age (e.g. contortions, overgrowth). Use illustrative figures if complex.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zooecium morphology
rubrics_metrics.description: Record zooecia shape and proportions (e.g. 'elongate and slender, flattened on the ventral, strongly convex on the dorsal surface; rather deep in proportion to their breadth; the ectocyst colourless...; dorsal keel and furrow as a rule absent; orifice unusually inconspicuous, situated on a tubercle on the dorsal surface').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe surface profile, relative depth/breadth, ectocyst transparency/colour, dorsal/ventral features, and orifice position and conspicuousness. Note typical variation and exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polypide characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe internal/soft-part morphology of the polypide (e.g. 'Polypide stout and short; the tip of the fundus of the stomach capable of very complete constriction; the retractor muscles unusually short and stout').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include details of polypide shape, stomach fundus behavior, muscle configuration, and any unusual musculature that aids diagnosis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statoblast presence and morphology
rubrics_metrics.description: Report presence/absence and form of statoblasts (e.g. 'Only free statoblasts have been observed. They resemble those of S. indica, but are perhaps a little longer and more elongate').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note whether statoblasts are free or fixed, their morphology relative to related species, and any inferences about reproduction or development drawn from them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genus-level diagnostic characters and revisions
rubrics_metrics.description: State the essential characters that define the genus and how the new species affects that diagnosis (e.g. 'the essential character of the genus... is the differentiation of the proximal part of some or all of the zooecia to form stolon-like tubules. From Stephanella it is distinguished by the absence of a gelatinous covering, and by the fact that all the zooecia are attached...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide explicit genus-level traits, and if discovery of new species requires modification of the generic diagnosis, state the modification and the comparative basis for it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type specimen information and deposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify type material and its repository (e.g. 'TYPES in the Indian Museum').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declare holotype/lectotype/syntypes, their repository (museum), locality data, and any catalogue or accession numbers where available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Habitat and locality data
rubrics_metrics.description: Record habitat, exact locality, altitude, collector, and date (e.g. 'HABITAT. Malwa Tal, Kumaon (alt. 3600 feet), W. Himalayas (Kemp, May 1911)').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide precise geographic and ecological context (lake name, substrate, altitude), collector and date, and note substrates to which colonies were attached (stones, twigs, leaves).

rubrics_metrics.name: Biological and developmental observations
rubrics_metrics.description: Report biological state of specimens (e.g. presence of few statoblasts, condition of growth, development of new polyparia from statoblasts; 'They contained few statoblasts and were evidently in a condition of vigorous growth. Between the lateral branches new polyparia were developing...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include observations on reproductive state, growth vigor, attachment mode, and any developmental processes observed in situ or in collected material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intraspecific and geographic/seasonal variation
rubrics_metrics.description: Note variation between specimens from different localities or seasons (e.g. 'Specimens taken by Mr. Kemp... exhibit a somewhat greater tendency towards uprightness of the zooecia than those I found in autumn... The ectocyst is... of a deep but bright reddish-brown').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare material from multiple localities and seasons, document morphological and colour differences, and discuss implications for identification (forms, phases, or varietal names).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specimen preservation and figure preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: State methods of preservation and treatment used for specimens illustrated (e.g. 'preserved in spirit', 'preserved in formalin, stained with hæmalum, and after dehydration and clearing, mounted in canada balsam'; include magnification '× 30', and purpose of figure such as 'to show method of branching').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide preservation medium, staining protocol, mounting medium, magnification, and why the figure was made (what structural feature it shows). This informs reproducibility and interpretation of figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plate and caption conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Figure captions should include specimen name, locality, preservation method, magnification, and what is being shown (e.g. 'Fig. 1. Vertical branch of a polyparium of P. emarginata... (× 8). The specimen was preserved in formalin, stained with hæmalum, ... mounted in canada balsam.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write captions that allow a reader to understand the figure without referring back to the text: identify taxon, provenance, preparation, scale, and anatomical focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing and formatting conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: State indexing and typographical conventions used (e.g. 'All names printed in italics are synonyms.' 'Bold page numbers in the index are surrounded by tildes, e.g. ~76~.' 'In the Systematic Index, sub-family items were renumbered...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declare how synonyms, emphasis, and cross-references are indicated in the index and text so users can interpret entries correctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transcription/editorial correction standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Document editorial choices in preparing the text for publication/digital conversion (e.g. 'Greek letters used as symbols are spelled out, e.g. alpha, beta, etc.'; 'Letters missing or mis-typeset were inserted'; list of specific corrected typos).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When producing editions or transcriptions, record what systematic changes were made (spelling corrections, moved footnotes, punctuation standardization, restored characters) to preserve provenance and allow users to distinguish editorial emendations from original text.
